descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-92579 AC 2; UAT TC-24 ER 5 · “Deleting a patient removes all of that patient's data immediately (hard delete, not hidden)”. Mixed: stated part — every patient-linked row gone on the first read, earlier PHI_READ audit row kept; our part — a new delete audit row, the control patient's rows unchanged (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Decision D5 · S0 · Daniela

After a patient is deleted, a Quick Dictation box with their name, room and dictated text remains — delete it too?; and a deleted patient's unsent text stays in another device's draft store until sign-out (Q10)

Other cases of the same question (counted once): TC-25/S17

Approach · TC-01 Patient Chart Card · S20 Hard delete is immediate and complete in both contexts; the earlier access trail stays; the neighbour is untouched

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T2 Deleting a patient removes all of that patient's data immediately (hard delete, not hidden); the audit log of who accessed the chart is kept. (TFA-92579 AC 2; UAT TC-24)
  • U8 With multiple patients loaded, everything above holds in both Hospital and Nursing Home. (UAT TC-01; UAT 3.3)

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given Per context, a target and a control patient. Hospital target: pre-round text, a task, a medication row and a Quick Dictation placement. NH target: pre-round text, a task and a medication row (Quick Dictation is Hospital only). access.logChartAccess called on each target, so a PHI_READ row exists

When Delete each target through rounding:remove / snf:remove, and once more through the card's trash icon → OK (when S17's runner exists); read the backend on the first query after the mutation returns (no sweep, no cron)

Then get(id) is null; zero rows reference the id in every patient-linked table; audit_logs by_patient(id) = count before + 1 delete row and the earlier PHI_READ row is still there; the control patient's rows are unchanged

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): AC 2 'immediately (hard delete, not hidden)' + 'audit log … kept'. A deleted flag, a removed list row with the document left behind, a cascaded PHI_READ row, or a changed control row fails. Whether the Quick Dictation compartment text itself must go (not only its assignment) is TC-24 Q6. Hospital UI half overlaps TC-24 S13; …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method API · API (Convex functions); lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S20 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row; to be decided by Daniela.

Issue type: Needs a decision (Daniela) · environment local · tickets TFA-92579 ready for qa

After a physician deletes a Hospital patient, the chart and its data are gone, but Quick Dictation still shows a box labelled with that patient's room and full name, holding what was dictated for them.

Evidence: newspec-a (API and card trash -> OK). The Nursing Home half passes; the audit trail is kept and the control patient is unchanged. A quickDictationDrafts row keeps assignedPatientId = the deleted id plus the label '412 · <name>' and the text, because deleteRoundingPatient never touches quickDictationDrafts. This is exactly TC-24 Q6(a), which asks whether the box must go, and it is listed in the TC-24 risks. The leftover link to the deleted id fails the S20 oracle whatever Q6 decides; if Daniela agrees, Tim fixes it.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20 re-run), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: API · API (Convex functions); secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local (dev partial: get(id) null and missing from the list through user functions, as in S17); Source: newspec-c.
